experience.title: THE SEALED EXPRESS
experience.premise: On an interwar luxury night train, a famous jewel is discovered to be a replica after a tunnel blackout even though its locked display was never opened during the journey.
experience.player_question: How was the jewel replaced without opening the display during the journey, and why was the tunnel blackout made to look like the critical moment?
dramatic_spine: A blackout and alarm create an apparent impossible theft window.
GAMMA appears suspicious because he controls train procedure and is evasive.
A real procedural violation strengthens the false solution.
That secret cannot explain evidence that predates the journey.
BETA helps reframe the question from how the case was opened to when the real jewel last certainly existed.
A pre-departure record proves the replica was already present.
ALPHA's precision becomes evidence of privileged pre-departure access and knowledge.
The player accuses the man whose ROLE was built around protecting the jewel.
experience.truth: ALPHA replaced the real jewel with a replica before departure and used the tunnel alarm as theatrical misdirection to create a false crime window. GAMMA conceals an unrelated procedural violation. BETA is genuinely investigating.
experience.resolution: The player proves the jewel was already a replica before departure and identifies ALPHA as the person with the access and knowledge required to make the substitution.

role.label: Exhibition curator and diplomatic aide
role.description: Responsible for pre-departure preparation and publicly dedicated to order; actually the culprit.

role.label: Railway investigator
role.description: Official investigator whose person-centered instinct helps recover testimony other officials discount.

role.label: Chief conductor
role.description: Controls train procedure while bending one rule for an unrelated reason, becoming the initial red herring.

facts.proposition: The display seals remained intact throughout the journey.
The jewel inside the display after the tunnel is a replica.
A pre-departure image already shows the replica rather than the authenticated original.
The substitution occurred during the tunnel blackout.
GAMMA violated a train procedure during the journey.
ALPHA had custody-level access before the display was sealed for departure.
ALPHA demonstrates unusually precise knowledge of a distinctive feature of the authenticated original.
ALPHA replaced the real jewel before departure.
The tunnel alarm creates a memorable time boundary but does not prove physical access to the jewel.

relations.description: If the replica is visible before departure, the tunnel cannot be the substitution window.
Continuous seals push the meaningful access window before the journey.
ALPHA had the required pre-sealing opportunity.
ALPHA's privileged knowledge supports direct handling of the original.
GAMMA's on-train procedural violation cannot explain a pre-departure substitution.

opportunities.description: Expose GAMMA's procedural violation and create the first false solution.
Discover that the replica predates the tunnel event.
Reject the tunnel as the true substitution window.
Use pre-departure timing, opportunity, and privileged knowledge to identify ALPHA.

completion_conditions.description: Prove the tunnel was a false crime window and identify ALPHA as the pre-departure culprit.
